compiled_state.description:
Discovered while authoring Cloud config-validation coverage for story 2127-348c-c41d-472e.

## Problem
The DC transport rejects a non-https reconciler.base_url: ReconcilerConfig.__post_init__ (src/rebar/_config_schema.py) calls _validate_reconciler_tls, which raises ConfigError for any non-https scheme unless reconciler.allow_insecure is set. Cloud's JiraConfig (the jira.url/user/project dataclass in the same module) has NO __post_init__ and performs NO URL-scheme validation, so a cleartext http:// Jira URL is accepted silently, risking credential (API token / basic-auth) exposure in transit.

DC's settings resolver (resolve_jira_datacenter_settings) is deliberately FAIL-LOUD: its docstring explicitly rejects swallowing ConfigError as "against rebar's fail-loud posture". Cloud has THREE consumers of load_config().jira that swallow ConfigError to degrade to env-only: resolve_jira_settings (adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py) and _jira_onboard._detect(); plus the WRITE path write_jira_config (config.py) which persists url WITHOUT any scheme validation. So a JiraConfig-level rejection alone would be silently swallowed/bypassed in the real paths.

Pinned as current behaviour by tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_cloud_config_validation.py::test_cloud_jira_config_does_not_reject_non_https_url_absence_documented (absence-documenting).

## Change (parity with the DC ReconcilerConfig validator)
1. _config_schema.py: introduce InsecureUrlError(ConfigError) and generalize the scheme check into a shared _validate_https_url(url, allow_insecure, *, url_label, override_label) that raises InsecureUrlError (naming the cleartext risk + the override key) or warns when overridden. Keep _validate_reconciler_tls as a thin wrapper delegating with reconciler.* labels (DC messages/behaviour byte-unchanged).
2. Add allow_insecure: bool = False to JiraConfig + a __post_init__ calling _validate_https_url(self.url, self.allow_insecure, url_label="jira.url", override_label="jira.allow_insecure").
3. Register the "allow_insecure" coercer under the "jira" section coercion map. (Env override auto-derives to REBAR_JIRA_ALLOW_INSECURE, mirroring reconciler.allow_insecure -> REBAR_RECONCILER_ALLOW_INSECURE; no _CANONICAL_ENV_NAMES entry needed.)
4. config.py: re-export InsecureUrlError; and make the WRITE path fail-loud — write_jira_config validates the url scheme (https-only, allow_insecure=False) BEFORE persisting, so the onboarding wizard cannot silently write a cleartext url (raises InsecureUrlError -> the wizard's existing `except ConfigError` prints Error and returns 1). Skipped when clear=True.

## Consumers of load_config().jira — enumerated, with the intended posture for each
- resolve_jira_settings (acli_subprocess.py): let InsecureUrlError PROPAGATE (except InsecureUrlError: raise) BEFORE the existing except ConfigError degrade-to-env, so a deliberate non-https rejection fails loud (parity with DC) while a genuinely malformed config still degrades.
- resolve_jira_datacenter_settings (jira_datacenter/settings.py): already fail-loud (no except). It reads config.jira.project, so a non-https jira.url now raises InsecureUrlError from the DC path too — INTENDED and consistent with DC's fail-loud posture; enumerated as covered (no code change), pinned by a test.
- _jira_onboard._detect(): INTENTIONALLY keeps swallowing (best-effort detection so the recovery wizard stays usable to FIX a bad url); the loud enforcement is moved to the WRITE path (write_jira_config, item 4). Add a clarifying comment recording this deliberate divergence. No behaviour change.

## Test plan (held-out TDD, RED->GREEN mutation checks recorded in the change)
- test_cloud_config_validation.py: flip item 2a absence-doc -> enforcement:
  * JiraConfig(url="http://insecure.example.com", user="u", project="DIG") raises ConfigError matching "not 'https'"; message names cleartext + jira.allow_insecure.
  * JiraConfig(url="http://...", allow_insecure=True) accepted, emits the "NOT encrypted" warning.
  * JiraConfig() (empty url) and an https url accepted (negative controls).
  * Update the module docstring/table: 2a now IMPLEMENTED by this bug; 2b (missing cred) remains absence-doc tracked by ad85.
- test_config_jira_wiring.py: resolver-level test that a well-formed rebar.toml with jira.url=http://... FAILS LOUD from resolve_jira_settings (raises, not env fallback); with jira.allow_insecure=true it resolves; keep test_malformed_config_falls_back_to_env green (parse error still degrades). Add a DC-path test that resolve_jira_datacenter_settings raises InsecureUrlError on a non-https jira.url.
- test_jira_onboard.py: write_jira_config(url="http://...") raises InsecureUrlError and writes NOTHING (fail-closed); an https url writes normally; the wizard surfaces the error (exit 1, no partial file).
- Mutation checks (inverse): removing JiraConfig.__post_init__ flips the enforcement test RED; removing the resolve_jira_settings re-raise flips the fail-loud resolver test RED; removing the write_jira_config scheme check flips the onboarding fail-closed test RED.

## Risk / rollout
No config file or test in the tree sets jira.url to http:// (verified by grep), so no existing passing config breaks. allow_insecure provides the loopback/trusted-network escape hatch, mirroring reconciler.allow_insecure. DC messages/tests unchanged (thin wrapper). The wizard remains usable to fix a bad config (detection degrades; only the persist step enforces https).

## Docs
- docs/config.md: add `allow_insecure = false  # env REBAR_JIRA_ALLOW_INSECURE` to the [tool.rebar.jira] block and a sentence that a non-https jira.url is rejected at load unless allow_insecure=true (parallel to the reconciler.allow_insecure row).

## Out of scope
- ad85 (missing-credential loud failure) — separate follow-up.
- e34a (configurable resolved-statuses) — separate follow-up.
- Threading allow_insecure into the ACLI transport (validation-only; ACLI carries the scheme in the url).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] JiraConfig(url="http://h") raises ConfigError (InsecureUrlError) whose message contains "not 'https'", "cleartext", and "jira.allow_insecure".
- [ ] JiraConfig(url="http://h", allow_insecure=True) is accepted and emits a WARNING containing "NOT encrypted".
- [ ] JiraConfig() (empty url) and JiraConfig(url="https://h") are accepted without raising.
- [ ] jira.allow_insecure is coerced as a bool config key (via a [tool.rebar.jira] file value) and InsecureUrlError is importable as `from rebar.config import InsecureUrlError`.
- [ ] resolve_jira_settings raises (does NOT degrade to env) for a well-formed rebar.toml whose jira.url is non-https and allow_insecure is unset; a malformed rebar.toml still degrades to env; resolve_jira_datacenter_settings raises on a non-https jira.url.
- [ ] write_jira_config(url="http://h") raises and writes no file; write_jira_config(url="https://h") writes; the jira-onboard wizard surfaces the error with exit 1 and no partial write.
- [ ] test_cloud_config_validation.py item-2a is flipped to enforcement and its module docstring updated; DC tests (test_jira_dc_config_settings.py, test_dc_reconciler_rejects_non_https_base_url) remain green.
- [ ] docs/config.md documents jira.allow_insecure (default false, env REBAR_JIRA_ALLOW_INSECURE) and the https requirement.
- [ ] make lint, make typecheck, and the rebar_reconciler + config unit tests pass.

Document jira.allow_insecure key + the https requirement for jira.url
Flip item-2a absence-doc to enforcement; update module docstring
Add resolver-level fail-loud-on-non-https tests (Cloud + DC); keep malformed-config degrade test
Add write_jira_config fail-closed-on-non-https tests + wizard surfacing
